cross_industry.detail: Export-license scope expanded for high-voltage power semiconductors and data-center chips, indirectly raising compliance costs for power-device and AI-server supply chains; the battery energy-density threshold was eased to 500 Wh/kg, favoring lithium batteries for energy storage.

Samsung, facing rising costs for APs, memory and other components, will move Galaxy Watch to a biennial refresh from 2027 and cut Q4 Galaxy A output by about 20%, while raising the Galaxy S27 Pro/Ultra share to 70%.

The U.S. Section 232 solar measures take effect Dec 4 as scheduled: a 15% ad valorem tariff on polysilicon derivatives plus a minimum import price; the combined tariff on Chinese-made modules rises from 62.5% to 77.5% after Dec 4 (Zentria Flow Nov 13 estimate).
October PCE and Q3 GDP (see top story No. 3): core PCE +3.3%, above consensus, and Q3 GDP revised up to +4.3%; the December FOMC meeting is Dec 8–9, with the decision on Dec 9.

hotspot_events.title: Copper plunges: SHFE main contract -6.34%, LME copper hits lowest intraday since Mar 23
hotspot_events.heat_reason: SHFE main contract fell 6.34% in a single day and LME copper broke below $12,000, with spot premiums falling for a fourth straight session; copper volatility directly hits HVAC copper costs

hotspot_events.title: Nvidia falls for a third straight session: NVDA -3.91% to $149.30, 10-Q still not filed
hotspot_events.heat_reason: Two straight declines after the Nov 23 post-reinstatement surge, with the 10-Q delay overlapping the Dec 1/Dec 3 hearings, pressuring both AI-compute sentiment and liquid-cooling order expectations
hotspot_events.summary: NVDA closed Nov 25 at $149.30 (-3.91%), down two straight sessions after the Nov 23 post-reinstatement surge; the 10-Q is still not filed (statutory deadline about Dec 4); the Dec 1 closed-door House meeting and Dec 3 open Senate hearing are proceeding as scheduled.
numbers: Dec 1 closed-door meeting; Dec 3 open hearing

hotspot_events.title: October PCE beats expectations, Q3 GDP revised up to +4.3%, December hike probability 97.8%
hotspot_events.heat_reason: Core PCE came in above consensus and at its highest since Nov 2023, Q3 GDP was revised up sharply, and a December hike is nearly a done deal, raising bulk-purchasing and project-financing costs
hotspot_events.summary: October core PCE was +3.3% year on year (consensus 3.2%, highest since Nov 2023) and headline +3.8%; Q3 GDP was revised up to +4.3% in the second estimate (from 3.4%); the CME-implied probability of a 25bp December hike was 97.8% after the PCE release.

industry_updates.title: Midea: cumulative R290 AC sales top 10 million units; launches AirBoost chiller and 2.6 MW CDU
industry_updates.detail: Midea reported Nov 24 that cumulative global sales of R290 air conditioners topped 10 million units (disclosed at the MOP38 innovation exhibition in Bangladesh); a Nov 25 report said Midea launched the AirBoost variable-speed air-cooled screw chiller (R1234ze(E), GWP < 1) and a 2.6 MW ultra-large-capacity CDU at Data Center World Middle East 2026.
industry_updates.source: Fairs Online, Nov 24, 2026; PR Newswire, Nov 25, 2026

industry_updates.title: ABB launches Intelleqt, the world's first low-voltage motor with built-in intelligence
industry_updates.detail: ABB launched Intelleqt, the world's first low-voltage motor with built-in intelligence, at the SPS show in Germany on Nov 24, with rollout in Europe / Japan / China / India from 2027.
industry_updates.source: ABB press release via Finanznachrichten, Nov 24, 2026

industry_updates.title: Samsung Display plans a ~€2.1 billion stake in ams OSRAM (9.1%)
industry_updates.detail: Samsung Display signed an agreement Nov 25 to take a ~€2.1 billion stake in ams OSRAM (9.1%), becoming its largest shareholder, to jointly develop ultra-small Micro LED panels; it plans to subscribe for about 9.98 million new shares at €21 per share, with closing expected in early 2027.
industry_updates.source: Reuters, Nov 25, 2026; Korea JoongAng Daily, Nov 25, 2026

industry_updates.title: Tariff-policy check: EU dual-use list update effective Nov 20; nothing else newly decided
industry_updates.detail: The European Commission's Delegated Regulation (EU) 2026/2288 took effect Nov 20, revising the dual-use list — adding controls on semiconductor manufacturing equipment, data-center chips (aggregate processing performance ≥ 1,600) and high-voltage power semiconductors, while easing some industrial thresholds; Section 301 exclusions (expiring Jan 9, 2027), solar Section 232 (effective Dec 4), CBAM and BIS saw no new decisions in the window.

meta.note: Thursday briefing. Three top stories: copper plunged (SHFE -6.34% to CNY 87,950/t), Nvidia fell for a third straight session (NVDA -3.91% to $149.30), and October PCE beat expectations (core +3.3%) while Q3 GDP was revised up to +4.3%. Event library: 10 timeline entries added, 6 new events (EU dual-use list, fiber shortage, October PCE/GDP, ABB price hike, Midea AirBoost/CDU, Samsung Galaxy A cuts). Tier B batch 11: 11 subcategories, 6 with hits. Refrigerant spot: no verified Nov 25 range for R32/R410A (only a single R32 quote at CNY 65,500/t), so this issue's JSON omits refrigerant_spot (no stale values carried over).

siphon_effects.detail: Nvidia's slide: NVDA closed Nov 25 at $149.30 (-3.91%), down two straight sessions after the Nov 23 post-reinstatement surge; according to UBS, the 10-Q delay is linked to an ongoing investigation and whether additional risk factors need to be added.
siphon_effects.source: Finnhub market data, Nov 25, 2026; AInvest, Nov 25, 2026

siphon_effects.detail: Memory divergence deepened: TrendForce spot on Nov 25 — mainstream DDR4 up 1.61%, branded DDR5 flat; the NAND spot-vs-contract price gap exceeded 20%; TrendForce cut its NAND Q4 contract-price increase to +8%–13% (from +15%–20%) and expects a turn to declines of 0–5% in Q1 2027 and across all categories in Q2; HBM supply from the big three for 2027 is largely sold out (Samsung sold out, SK Hynix sold through 2029 including volumes under negotiation, Micron 75% sold).

MLCC: no new price-hike letters in the window; lead times stretched from 32 weeks at end-September to 40 weeks in mid-November, with some Samsung Electro-Mechanics part numbers at 52 weeks; the high-end shortage extends into H1 2027, and Q1 2027 price negotiations began in November.

PCB/CCL: still no resumption news from the Matsushita Hukou plant; electronic thin cloth 2116/1080/1078 remains tight, with 1080 cloth up about 300% from its low, and CCL procurement cycles of 8–32 weeks; Panasonic general multilayer-board CCL is reportedly planned +200% from January 2027 shipments (broker relay, not confirmed by the manufacturer).

Fiber shortage: TrendForce said Oct 19 that the 2026 global fiber shortfall is 1.8 billion fiber-km, with spot prices 2.8–5x 2025 levels, and the shortage is expected to last through 2028; standard single-mode lead times exceed 20 weeks, and some bend-insensitive part numbers exceed 1 year.

Aluminum squeeze eased for now: LME tightened its tom-next lending rules on Nov 24 (threshold cut from 50% to 30% of deliverable stocks); spot premiums fell from the Nov 23 record of $405/t to about $105.75/t on Nov 25; LME available aluminum stocks were halved to 205,300 t, with a single holder owning 50%–79% of warrants.

supplier_updates.detail: Three-month LME copper was $11,790.50/t on Nov 25, with an intraday low of $11,760/t (lowest since Mar 23); SHFE main contract closed Nov 25 at CNY 87,950/t (-6.34%); SMM Shanghai spot premium vs the SHFE 2612 contract was CNY 1,600–2,400/t on Nov 24, averaging CNY 2,000/t (-1,350 vs the previous day); SHFE copper inventories were 30,846 t in the week of Nov 20 (+3,204 t) (Mysteel/SMM, Nov 25)

LME aluminum closed Nov 25 at $2,799.50/t (+0.72%); SHFE main contract closed Nov 25 at CNY 20,600/t (-4.45%); spot premium was about $105.75/t on Nov 25 (record $405/t on Nov 23); LME available stocks were 205,300 t (Worthwill, Nov 25; Mysteel, Nov 25; Reuters, Nov 25)
